title: Interactive Policy Lens for Batching & Cache Explainability
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Overview:
Design an "Interactive Policy Lens" within the Redwood Console that surfaces concise, actionable explanations for batching and caching recommendations. The lens should help engineers and platform owners understand why a given recommendation was suggested, the expected latency and cost delta, the confidence level, and safe rollout/guardrail options. It must live on the per-route and per-model configuration page and be accessible from the Optimize recommendations hub.

Goals:
- Make batching/cache recommendations (automatic and manual) transparent and debuggable.
- Reduce friction for adoption by showing concrete trade-offs (requests/sec, p95 latency, estimated token cost).
- Provide conservative guardrail defaults and one-click safe rollouts (canary, staged ramp, immediate).
- Offer a simulation preview for short-history workloads to surface regressions before rollouts.

Core interactions and components proposed:
1) Recommendation Summary Card: single-line recommendation (e.g., "Enable prefix KV cache for /chat-completion") with three compact indicators: estimated cost delta, latency impact, confidence band (low/med/high). Each indicator is hoverable with short microcopy.
2) Expandable Policy Lens Panel: a right-rail overlay that opens with full explainers: why this recommendation, rule provenance (heuristic vs. learned), sample traces affected, and the top-3 tokens/requests that would benefit.
3) Simulation Playground: run the proposal against recent route traces (last 1k requests) with a fast approximate replay and show token-level differences, expected throughput changes, and failure modes (cache misses, increased prefix mismatch).
4) Guardrail Controls: prefilled rollout presets (safe-canary: 5% ramp, staged-ramp: 25/50/100, instant) with suggested monitoring hooks (p95 latency alert, error-rate spike threshold, perplexity drift).
5) Quick Revert & Fallback: one-click fallback to previous model or to smaller batch sizes with automatic rollback if thresholds are crossed.
6) Explainability notes: a human-readable rationale and an engineering rationale (short bullet list) plus links to the kernel/runtime constraints that motivated the suggestion.

Design constraints and considerations:
- Keep the lens lightweight for frequent use: default collapsed card, pay-to-open detail panel.
- Avoid exposing proprietary kernel heuristics; instead surface behavioral evidence (traces, histograms).
- Provide conservative defaults for customer workloads with high regulatory needs.
- Ensure accessibility for keyboard and screen-reader interactions.
- Minimize cognitive overload: show most impactful metrics first and hide advanced metrics behind an "Advanced" toggle.

Success criteria (proposed):
- 30% increase in adoption of Optimize recommendations within 90 days of launch for low-risk routes.
- Reduce rollback rate for batching/caching changes by 40% via simulation preview and guardrails.
- Positive qualitative feedback from at least three enterprise customers during beta.

Dependencies and risks:
- Requires access to recent route traces and lightweight replay infra (eng dependency ENG-4987).
- Needs runtime endpoints to compute cost delta estimates and confidence score (research dependency RES-212).
- Privacy: replay must be redacted to avoid leaking user content; coordinate with security/compliance.
- Simulation accuracy: if the replay is too approximate, false confidence may increase risk of regressions.

Attachments and artifacts:
- Link to high-fidelity prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/Policy-Lens-Prototype
- PRD draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Policy+Lens+for+Batching+%26+Cache
- Measurement spec: https://docs.redwood.ai/optimize/sim-playbook

Technical notes for implementation team:
- The panel should request precomputed aggregates (cost_delta_estimate, confidence_score, sample_traces_id) rather than pulling raw traces in the UI. This avoids long client-side processing.
- Simulation should accept a sampled trace bundle (<= 1000 requests) and return a summary: { delta_tokens_saved, delta_cost_est, p95_latency_change, observed_failure_modes } (API contract to be designed with infra).

Open questions for review:
- Should we expose the full "rule provenance" (exact kernel heuristics) to enterprise customers under an advanced toggle, or keep that internal?
- How aggressive should the default confidence threshold be for auto-applying recommendations?
- Is 1k recent requests sufficient for meaningful simulation on bursty routes?

Next steps and delivery plan:
- UX: finalize visual spec and microcopy (due 2026-03-12).
- Research: produce a confidence score computation proposal and simulation accuracy SLA (due 2026-03-05).
- Engineering: API contract for the precomputed aggregates + replay endpoint (blocking, ENG-4987).
- Beta: launch with 3 internal services + 2 willing enterprise customers (target 2026-04-15).
comments: 2026-02-21 - Kickoff: cross-functional intro with PM (Diego Morales) and Eng (Sofia Ramos). Aligned on primary goals: explainability and safe rollouts.
2026-02-25 - Wireframes posted to Figma. Initial feedback from design review: reduce vertical height of the lens and prioritize sample traces over raw histograms.
2026-03-01 - PM review (Diego): ask to surface cost delta in USD for quick decision-making; add a tooltip with the exact token pricing assumptions.
2026-03-03 - Eng sync (Sofia): noted a dependency on the trace sampling API (ENG-4987) and suggested we precompute confidence_score in batch to avoid live computation costs.
2026-03-07 - Accessibility review (Maya Singh): add visible focus outlines, ARIA labels for the simulation controls, and ensure color contrast for risk bands.
2026-03-09 - Security note (Jerome Ackers): replay must redact PII; proposed adding a manifest of fields to strip. Marking for compliance review before beta.
2026-03-10 - Design handoff: high-fidelity prototype link shared. Requesting engineering estimation for simulation endpoint and precompute pipeline.
decisions: Prefer precomputed aggregates over raw trace fetching for the main panel (reduces latency and client work).
Default rollout preset will be 'safe-canary' (5% ramp) for first-time adopters unless user explicitly picks instant).
Expose human-readable rationale and a short engineer rationale; do not expose low-level kernel heuristics by default.
